I don’t have real‑time access to live air‑quality feeds, so I can’t tell you the exact AQI for Los Angeles at this moment. However, you can quickly find up‑to‑date information from a few reliable sources:

| Source | How to Check |
|--------|--------------|
| **EPA AirNow** | Visit <https://www.airnow.gov/> and enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code. It shows the current AQI, pollutant levels (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, O₃, NO₂, CO), and health advisories. |
| **AirVisual / IQAir** | Go to <https://www.iqair.com/usa/california/los-angeles> or <https://www.airvisual.com/>. They provide a live map, hourly forecasts, and historical trends. |
| **Weather Apps** | Many weather apps (e.g., Weather Underground, AccuWeather, The Weather Channel) include an AQI widget for major cities. |
| **Local News** | TV stations or local news websites often report on air‑quality alerts during smog events. |

If you’re looking for a quick snapshot, you can also use a voice assistant (Google Assistant, Siri, Alexa) and ask, “What’s the air quality in Los Angeles?” They pull data from the same public sources.

Let me know if you’d like a deeper dive into what the AQI numbers mean or how to interpret specific pollutant readings!
